A1.justification: Both PDFs describe p-MoD and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Their shared methods and experiments can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, efficiency measurements, component ablations, token-retention experiments and a FastV comparison.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds component ablations, additional compression-method comparisons, 13B-model evaluations and visual-grounding results.

M1.justification: The architecture and three components remain, but Eqs. (2)-(4) replace the selected-token additive term X_i with T(X_i). V1's Figure 2 already depicts reweighting the transformer output, consistent with v2's equations. The PDFs do not resolve whether this represents an actual procedural change or correction of an inconsistent mathematical specification.

E1.justification: V2 retains the original 14 benchmarks, adds VQAv2 to the main evaluation, and introduces visual grounding on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+ and RefCOCOg in Appendix A.2. Grounding substantially extends task requirements beyond the earlier question-answering and multimodal-understanding evaluations. The training datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's dense baselines and FastV comparison, v2 evaluates MQT and LLaVolta in Table 5; SparseVLM, VisionZip, PyramidDrop, FasterVLM, FreeVideoLLM, iLLaVA and LLaVA-PruMerge in Table 10; and concurrent γ-MoD in Table 11. These are substantial additions to the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: V2 adds a 13B-model evaluation and visual-grounding validation protocols using ACC@0.5. Figure 3 replaces the fixed 15% retention perturbation with retention-ratio sweeps across shallow, middle and deep layers. Ablation and efficiency tables also report different benchmark subsets, making their averages noncomparable across versions. The original 7B training recipe is retained.

E4.justification: V2's Table 3 adds a cumulative, equal-computation ablation of TanhNorm, STRing and PRD. Figure 3 expands the depth-redundancy investigation from one lowered retention setting to sensitivity curves. Conversely, v1's isolated STRing-removal row is no longer reported. The token-selection visualizations in Figures 5 and 6 retain the same evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. V2 adds results without introducing uncertainty estimation; its use of 'significantly' does not establish statistical testing.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive comparator, VQAv2, 13B, grounding and ablation results while preserving the shared main benchmark scores. Reported default KV-cache usage changes from 53.8% to 53.7%. TextVQA latency changes from 5191 to 519.1 ms for the baseline and 3680 to 368.0 ms for default p-MoD, without an explained timing-protocol change; these are revised values, not established speedups. V1's FastV latency and GPU-memory results are removed.

T1.justification: The selected-token definitions in Eqs. (2)-(4) change algebraically from adding X_i to adding T(X_i), rather than merely changing notation. The routing and cosine-decay definitions remain, and the unchanged clipping equation moves to Appendix D.3. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain TanhNorm, STRing and progressive ratio decay, with the claim that p-MoD preserves baseline performance while reducing training and inference costs. The additional evaluations support these retained claims without redefining the principal contribution or proposed mechanism.

C2.justification: V2 adds discussion of OCR sensitivity, repeated scaling as an overflow mechanism, grounding performance losses, and the requirement for training or continued fine-tuning rather than training-free deployment. It removes v1's extensive argument that attention-score pruning is incompatible with FlashAttention. The earlier single-image applicability limitation is retained in Appendix C.3.

D1.justification: Training hyperparameters, hardware, encoder-freezing policies and code/data links are largely retained after relocation. However, v2 drops the detailed FastV pruning and attention-implementation settings, the explanation of retraining on released 779K rather than original 760K data, and the explicit MME normalization instruction. These are documentation losses, not established changes to the underlying settings.

R1.justification: V2 substantially broadens positioning around query-based compression, token merging and newer pruning methods. Appendix A.4 newly acknowledges concurrent γ-MoD and distinguishes its layer-selection approach from p-MoD. The earlier FlashAttention-based criticism and associated citations are removed, changing an important part of the comparison with prior work.

P1.justification: V2 revises the abstract, introduction and conclusion, reorders the experimental subsections, and promotes method comparisons into the main text. The appendix is substantially reorganized into experiments, visualization, discussion and implementation sections. Hardware information, limitations and PRD clipping are relocated; author and affiliation text also changes.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn from a four-bar experiment into retention-ratio curves, and Figure 1's radar display is updated. Main benchmark tables are regrouped from seven-plus-seven to ten-plus-five benchmarks, ablation tables are reorganized, and several comparison tables are added. The appendix layout changes substantially, while Figures 5 and 6 preserve their original image content.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's narrow comparison against alternative compression methods through broader comparisons, including γ-MoD, and strengthens component validation with cumulative ablations and retention sweeps. The 13B and grounding experiments better test applicability, while grounding losses and the training requirement receive explicit qualification. These gains outweigh the lost FastV timing/memory documentation, although unexplained latency revisions and stale equation/table references in the overflow discussion remain reporting weaknesses.
